title: VPC/On-Prem Deployment Sprint Retro + Risk Map (Aug 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the Sprint retro for the VPC/On‑Prem installs stream (Sprint 42 cadence), compiles the recurring customer blockers we saw in the last 4 weeks, and produces a prioritized risk map with concrete mitigations and owners. Intended audience: private deployments eng, solutions engineering, SRE, and product leads.

Attendees:
- Asha Menon (owner)
- Gabe Torres (platform eng)
- Liang Zhao (networking)
- Maya Patel (solutions eng)
- Omar Hassan (sre)
- Observers: two PMs joined for impact context

High-level summary:
- Completed 6 customer handoffs; 4 were VPC, 2 on‑prem airgapped installs.
- Average install time slipped to 7.8 business days (target 5).
- Primary friction: network ACLs, customer-side NAT gateway config, and mismatch in OS package baseline for on‑prem nodes.
- Positive: telemetry instrumentation rollout reduced the time to reproduce a failed agent bootstrap from ~3 days to <6 hours for 3 customers.

What went well:
- Telemetry onboarding: the new debug mode flag produced actionable logs on first boot for 3 customers — saved ~10 engineer-hours each.
- Preflight checklist adoption: Solutions eng used the new checklist with two customers and caught an IP routing issue before onsite work.
- Canary of the slim-agent package succeeded on internal staging and one customer site with no regressions.

What didn't go well / recurring problems:
1) Networking assumptions: customers frequently have restrictive egress rules or split-horizon DNS. Our default preflight misses some of these patterns (see sample from OrionHealth).
2) OS baseline drift: older SLES/Ubuntu-LTS versions cause systemd unit failures for agent v1.12. We need a compatibility shim or documented fallback.
3) Credential handoffs: encrypted key exchange process is error-prone and not well integrated with customer KMS flows.
4) Resource wait-time transparency: customers expect ETA for quota approvals (cloud NICs, IPs). Lack of visibility causes long pauses.

Top customer blockers (last 4 weeks):
- AcmeFin (VPC): CIDR overlap + shared services VPC — had to rearchitect peering. Blocker status: mitigated, but added 5 days. Owner: Maya.
- OrionHealth (On‑prem): DNS split‑horizon, internal registry access blocked. Blocker status: active; workaround uses hostfile + proxy. Owner: Liang.
- LuminaRetail (VPC): egress-only security group for compliance; our build fetches during bootstrap failed. Blocker status: mitigated via preseeded artifacts. Owner: Gabe.
- NovaAnalytics (On‑prem airgap): hardware mismatch (NVMe vs expected SSD) causing I/O scheduler issues. Blocker status: active. Owner: Omar.

Incidents & root cause notes:
- Incident 2026-08-03: customer agent fails at systemd start on Debian 10. Root cause: unit file uses systemd 'DefaultDependencies=no' which interacts poorly with older kernel shim in Debian 10 cloud images. Workaround applied by adding ExecStartPre sleep and systemctl daemon-reload. Long-term fix: agent v1.13 unit file changes and preflight systemd check.
- Incident 2026-07-28: intermittent gRPC connection drops during heavy prefix caching. Root cause: kernel tuning (net.core.rmem_max) lower on some on‑prem hosts. Mitigation: document recommended sysctl and add a preflight sysctl check.

Telemetry / metrics we saw (signals to watch):
- Install duration histogram: median 3.2d, p95 12d.
- Agent bootstrap failure rate week-on-week: 7% -> 4% after debug mode rollout.
- Customer support RT: mean time to first triage down from 18h to 6h where telemetry was enabled.

Runbook and playbook changes proposed:
- Preflight checklist v2 (attached in linked artifacts): add sysctl table, DNS split-horizon probe, and explicit KMS pattern checklist. Owner: Liang. Due: 2026-08-20.
- Shipping a compatibility matrix for OS images + agent versions; include known bad kernel combos. Owner: Gabe. Due: 2026-08-25.
- Credential exchange doc: create standard workflows for AWS, Azure, and vault-based KMS. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-08-22.

Risk map (short form, prioritized):
- High impact / high likelihood: Customer network complexity (split-horizon DNS, private registries) -> reduces success rate and increases install time. Mitigation: expand preflight checks and ship sample resolver probe. Owner: Liang.
- High impact / medium likelihood: On‑prem hardware mismatches (storage/cpu features) -> can require onsite changes or rollback. Mitigation: include minimal hardware checklist + targeted agent fallback. Owner: Omar.
- Medium impact / medium likelihood: Credential handoff failures -> escalate to SRE for temporary proxy. Mitigation: credential exchange templates + support scripts. Owner: Maya.
- Low impact / low likelihood: Downstream dependency pulls blocked by egress policy -> mitigate by artifact pre-seeding and offline bundle. Owner: Gabe.

Open actions (owner — action — due):
- Liang — publish preflight v2 + tests for DNS probe — 2026-08-20.
- Gabe — compatibility matrix + staging run with Debian 10/11/12 across agent v1.12/v1.13 — 2026-08-25.
- Maya — credential exchange templates + Slack workflow for escalation — 2026-08-22.
- Omar — create quick reference for sysctl and storage tuning (2 pager) — 2026-08-19.
- Asha — organize a customer-patterns sync (solutions eng + support) to codify 5 common network patterns — 2026-08-18.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Move forward with debug-mode as default flag enabled for new installs for 30 days (opt-out for customers worried about logs).
- Short-term: add a hostfile-proxy workaround script to the archive for urgent splits — owner Liang.
- Long-term: plan a dedicated 'network compatibility' automation spike in sprint 43 to reduce install time variance.

Notes to follow-up on:
- Assess whether we should add a UI/exposed status for 'waiting on customer quota' to reduce back-and-forth with customers. Product + Solutions to scope by 2026-08-21.
- Evaluate cost of supporting more agent backward-compat shims vs raising minimum supported OS. Engineering to present tradeoffs.

Next review / sync:
- Quick sync in 1 week (2026-08-20) to review progress on preflight v2 and the compatibility matrix; full retro at end of sprint 43.

Appendix (examples shared in meeting):
- OrionHealth sample DNS trace (sanitized): A -> resolves internal-only host to 10.0.0.5, external NS unreachable from customer subnet.
- Excerpt of support thread: ENG-5123 (credential exchange failure) with timeline and attempted workarounds.

If you have additions or corrections, add comment inline or ping #private-deployments on Slack.
